cards.explanation: The answer is dew from the LORD. Micah says the remnant of Jacob will be "…like dew from the LORD…" in the midst of many peoples (Micah 5:7). Dew just shows up on the grass, quiet and gentle, and nobody has to order it. I think that's a lovely picture to open with, friends. Hold onto it, because the next picture is not so quiet.

The answer is False. Micah says the dew and showers "…do not wait for man or linger for mankind." (Micah 5:7). They don't hang around for anybody to give permission. They just arrive, and the grass is glad about it.

The answer is a lion among the forest beasts. Micah says the remnant will be "…like a lion among the beasts of the forest…" (Micah 5:8). A lion, friends! Not a gentle picture at all. Micah doesn't stay in one picture for long, and this one has teeth.

The answer is False. In the lion picture, Micah says the lion tramples and tears as it passes through "…with no one to rescue them." (Micah 5:8). The text says no one is there to rescue them. It's a heavy picture, so I'll just let the words stand.

The answer is that they will be cut off. Micah says, "Your hand will be lifted over your foes, and all your enemies will be cut off." (Micah 5:9). Notice the word "all," friends. The text doesn't say some of them. It says all your enemies.

The answer is chariots. The LORD says, "I will remove your horses from among you and wreck your chariots." (Micah 5:10). Horses and chariots go together, so He takes both. Chariots are the word that fills this blank.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "I will remove the cities of your land and tear down all your strongholds." (Micah 5:11). Both the cities and all the strongholds are named, friends. The text doesn't leave one standing in this verse.

The answer is fortune-tellers. The LORD says, "I will cut the sorceries from your hand, and you will have no fortune-tellers." (Micah 5:12). Sorceries go and fortune-tellers go with them. That's the word for the blank.

The answer is so the people stop bowing to their own handiwork. The LORD says, "I will also cut off the carved images and sacred pillars from among you, so that you will no longer bow down to the work of your own hands." (Micah 5:13). The reason is right there in the verse, friends. People were bowing to something their own hands made.

The answer is the nations that have not obeyed Him. The LORD says, "I will take vengeance in anger and wrath upon the nations that have not obeyed Me." (Micah 5:15). The text names one thing about these nations, that they have not obeyed Him. That's the whole description.
